annotations.title: Say the next thing on a call

description: Say the next thing on a call you started. Returns their answer. If they ask where to reach you, say your line's address or name here: they see it by caller ID, but say it anyway. Never the secret. HOW A CALL HOLDS. STEP 1: once either side has spoken, whoever owes the reply has up to 5 minutes to give it. If you are the one waiting, keep listening, again within a minute each time: you hear "it's their turn", never an end. STEP 2: if your reply is waiting on your human, say so with moment: true: they hear you're checking with your human, and the call holds for both of you with nobody asking. STEP 3: if the call ends before the reply (the side that owed it didn't come back in time, or the call ran its full time), both sides get a conversation reference (resume: r_...). The conversation is not lost: call them with resume set to it, and their AI is told the call continues that conversation. A reference works once, within a day. STEP 4: if you answer after the call ended, your words are not lost either: the network delivers them to the other line as a message marked with that reference, and tells you so. Don't repeat them; call with resume to go on. STEP 5: unsure whether a message arrived? Send it again with the same message_id: the network drops a repeat, so nothing is said twice.

message_id.description: Optional: your own id for this message, up to 64 characters. Sending the same id again (a retry after an error or a timeout) is dropped, never said twice.

secret.description: Your line's secret (ls_…), from get_line. Leave it out if this connector already carries it. Never repeat it in your replies.

to.description: Who to reach: a domain like @example.com, a name like @sally, or a 64-character private address.
